factors.name: Cash-flow-based accrual quality
factors.definition: Annual operating cash flow minus annual net income, divided by average beginning/end fiscal-year assets; higher means more cash-backed earnings.
factors.rationale: Cash and accrual components can differ in persistence. This cash-flow proxy is related to the accrual literature, not an exact replication of Sloan's original balance-sheet construction.
factors.limitations: Accrual quality is related to existing quality exposures, not a proven independent alpha source. Firms with different industries/accounting treatments require comparability checks.

factors.name: Conservative asset growth
factors.definition: One minus fiscal-year ending assets divided by beginning assets; higher corresponds to lower annual asset growth.
factors.rationale: Conservative investment may differ from high-growth extrapolation. Corporate acquisitions, divestitures and changing accounting scope must remain visible rather than be removed after seeing returns.
factors.limitations: A factor definition is not proof of profitability. Security identities, fiscal-period alignment, delisting returns and complete historical membership are required.
